scope: Live per-Connection Session codec planning and a separately authorized signed server-origin execution primitive. Required foundation for the unfinished Connect Session coordinator.
implementation: The controller-bound planner uses current peer capability declarations, preserves logical IDs and directions, applies soft codec preferences independently per peer, retains a compatible current format when preferred codecs are unavailable, and preserves unrelated/data bindings. It does not grandfather a withdrawn targeted format. Plans carry exact stream revision and capability declaration generation; no plan grants IO.

A distinct NativeSessionCodecPolicy supplies fresh exact host authority. The sealed typed codec invocation cannot borrow a subscription grant. Common server-offer mechanics share only request-slot serialization and signed exact parameter confirmation, and retain existing subscription-specific public policy and invocation types.

The executor reserves the physical peer request slot, bounds host authorization, rechecks exact origin/revision/declaration and invokes the existing atomic selected-media transaction. A no-change observation leaves the revision, resource budget and wire untouched. It invokes no subscription mutation API.

After actual Core success, the executor seals historical operation/scope/revision/binding metadata without retaining the physical origin or authorization reader. Revocation after a real commit cannot erase the observed success. Pre-Core refusal is explicitly no media effect; all errors after entering Core conservatively retain possible-effect classification. The executor never retries.

New actual QUIC and WebTransport cases verify signed offers and replies, unchanged old transport and decoded PCMU while awaiting confirmation, queued writer release without authority reentry, committed PCMA replacement with decoded output and old-handle refusal, no-op with unchanged budget/revision and no wire, duplicate operation refusal and historical outcome custody without retained readers. The failure case verifies current denial, a stale revision after signed mute/unmute, exact mismatched confirmation refusal, unchanged old transport and decoded PCMU recovery, and no automatic retry.

The16 existing transport regressions cover codec update, independent hold/mute controls, future Participant subscriptions and server-request lifetime/cancellation/uncertainty. The20 planner tests and13 current wire/golden tests also pass; all225 schema vectors remain current.

Keep the live refusal until this real coordinator is installed.
